app.name: HemoScan
app.disclaimerTitle: Screening tool — confirm with a blood test
app.disclaimer: HemoScan screens for the chance of anemia from photos of the eye, nails and palm. If it shows a chance of anemia, get a blood test (CBC) and talk to a doctor or health worker before starting any treatment.
app.disclaimerShort: Screens for the chance of anemia. Confirm with a blood test.

common.errorGeneric: Something went wrong. Please try again.

onboarding.step1Title: Hemoglobin check with your phone camera
onboarding.step1Body: HemoScan looks at the color of your inner eyelid, fingernails and palm to estimate your hemoglobin. No needles, no blood, and it works without internet.
onboarding.step2Body: Inner lower eyelid, fingernail beds and palm. The eyelid and nails work best for all skin tones. Scanning all three gives the most reliable result.
onboarding.step3Title: Screens for the chance of anemia
onboarding.step3Body: If HemoScan shows a chance of anemia, confirm it with a simple blood test at your nearest health centre before taking any medicine.

about.title: About HemoScan
about.how: HemoScan checks photo quality, corrects the lighting, finds the inner eyelid, nail beds or palm, and measures their color. A machine-learning model turns these color patterns into an estimated hemoglobin value, which is compared with WHO anemia thresholds for your age, sex and pregnancy status. Everything runs on your device.
about.privacy: Results are stored only on this device. Photos are not saved. Nothing is uploaded unless you turn on data contribution and sync in Settings.
about.limits: Use good daylight, remove nail polish, and avoid scanning during an eye infection or right after crying. HemoScan screens for the chance of anemia; a blood test confirms it.

conditions.title: Before you scan
conditions.subtitle: Tick anything that applies. These can make the area look redder or paler than your blood really is, so we give it less weight.

items.criedOrRubbed: I cried or rubbed my eyes in the last few hours
items.eyeIrritation: My eyes are red, itchy, infected or I used eye drops
items.nailPolishOrHenna: Nail polish, mehndi (henna) or stain on my nails
items.fingerInjury: A finger or nail is injured, bruised or swollen
items.nailsCutShort: I cut my nails very short in the last 2 days
items.coldHands: My hands are cold right now
items.hennaOnPalm: Mehndi (henna) or colour on my palm
items.hotWaterOrExercise: I just washed in hot water, exercised or did heavy work

effects.criedOrRubbed: Crying or rubbing makes the inner eyelid redder — anemia could be missed.
effects.eyeIrritation: Red or irritated eyes make the eyelid look redder than the blood is.
effects.nailPolishOrHenna: Polish or mehndi hides the nail bed colour.
effects.fingerInjury: An injury or bruise changes the nail colour.
effects.nailsCutShort: Freshly cut nails show more pale edge and can look anaemic when they are not.
effects.coldHands: Cold hands look paler because less blood flows to the skin.
effects.hotWaterOrExercise: Hot water or exercise makes the palm redder for a while.

imageFlags.scleraRed: Detected: the white of the eye looks red (crying, rubbing or irritation?).
imageFlags.nailCoating: Detected: colour on the nails that looks like polish or mehndi.
imageFlags.nailDarkSpot: Detected: a dark spot on a nail (bruise or injury?).
imageFlags.hennaDetected: Detected: colour on the palm that looks like mehndi.

adjustments.title: What we took into account
adjustments.allAffected: Every scanned area was affected (e.g. polish, crying). This estimate is only indicative — please scan again later or get a blood test.
adjustments.altitude: Living at altitude raises hemoglobin naturally (WHO). {{hb}} − {{adj}} = {{adjusted}} g/dL was compared with the anemia cutoff.
adjustments.palmLessWeight: palm reading given less weight, since pallor is harder to see on darker skin

population.eye: for your age group the eye reading gets a wider likely range and the other areas count more.
population.nails: for your age group the nail reading gets a wider likely range and the other areas count more.
population.palm: for your age group the palm check is used as a supporting check.

adjustments.outOfRange: this photo's camera or lighting is different from usual, so a wider likely range is shown. Adding a blood test result below makes future scans on this phone more precise.

calibration.intro: Got a lab hemoglobin result (CBC or HemoCue) taken within 7 days of this scan? Type it here — now or later from History. It makes future scans more accurate for this person, and teaches the app this phone's camera and lighting. This result itself stays as it was.

calibration.applied: Personally calibrated: {{offset}} g/dL from {{n}} of this person's blood tests (photo estimate before calibration: {{raw}} g/dL).
calibration.summary: Personal calibration: {{offset}} g/dL from {{n}} blood test(s)
calibration.none: No personal calibration yet. After a scan, you can enter a blood test result from the same week to calibrate.

errors.hbRange: Enter a hemoglobin value between 3 and 22 g/dL.
errors.tooFarApart: The blood test must be within 7 days of the scan — hemoglobin changes over weeks.

calibration.storedHelp: Used to make future scans more accurate for this person and on this phone.

learning.title: Learning from blood tests
learning.intro: Every blood test result you enter (from Results or History) is paired with that scan. HemoScan uses these pairs on this phone to correct for its camera and lighting. Nothing leaves the phone unless you export it.
learning.active: Learning is ON — on people it was not trained on, the average error dropped from {{before}} to {{after}} g/dL.
learning.needMore: Learning starts after {{n}} more blood test result(s).
learning.needPeople: Learning starts once blood tests from at least 2 different people are entered (one person's own tests already correct their scans).
learning.noImprovement: Not switched on yet: with the tests so far it did not lower the error ({{before}} → {{after}} g/dL). It is re-checked with every new blood test.
learning.applied: Learned from blood tests on this phone: {{offset}} g/dL applied ({{n}} test(s); photo estimate before correction: {{raw}} g/dL).
learning.exportEmpty: No scans with blood test results yet.
learning.exportHelp: Anonymous file (colour measurements, blood test value, age, sex, state — no names or photos). Send it to the HemoScan team to improve the model for everyone.

performance.title: Model performance
performance.intro: How the trained models scored on {{n}} people they had never seen (each person's photo was checked by a model trained without them), compared with their lab blood test.
performance.accuracyHeadline: accuracy for anemia / no anemia ({{n}} people)

help.accuracy: Share of people correctly marked as anemic or not anemic.
help.precision: Of the people marked as anemic, the share who really were.
help.recall: Of the people who really were anemic, the share the app caught.
help.specificity: Of the people without anemia, the share correctly marked as not anemic.
help.f1: Balance of precision and recall (1.0 = perfect).
help.auc: How well the estimate ranks people from most to least likely anemic (1.0 = perfect, 0.5 = chance).
help.r2: Share of the differences in hemoglobin between people that the estimate explains.

performance.palm: Palm check (anemia yes / no): AUC {{auc}}, finds {{sens}}% of anemic cases, {{spec}}% correct on non-anemic.
performance.method: Person-grouped 5-fold cross-validation on public research datasets with lab-measured hemoglobin; anemia uses the WHO 2011 cutoff for each person's age, sex and pregnancy.
